A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ATRIE and the same Legal Concept Entailment study. The text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original LCE experiments, ablations, human evaluations and efficiency measurements in Tables 1-6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds an expert comparison and manual hallucination check in Appendix E.3.

M1.justification: The retrieval, filtering, reason extraction, balancing and interpretation-generation pipeline remains unchanged, as do the LCE task and Appendix G prompts. Omission of voting details does not establish an actual method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Chinese case corpus and 16 concepts from 14 legal articles. The new Article 359 case study concerns a concept already included in Appendix H; it does not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Table 1, the Farui comparison and the appendix experiments are unchanged. Appendix E.3 compares ATRIE with the existing Direct Interpretation baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 adds a focused expert examination of paired interpretations and manual checking of ATRIE's cited cases against judgments. Existing LCE splits, models, metrics and temperatures remain documented consistently. The omission of v2's voting specification does not establish a switch to single-pass evaluation.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.3 examines why ATRIE and Direct Interpretation receive different human scores for Article 359 and checks whether their examples are grounded in actual judgments. Existing ablations, sensitivity analyses, model comparisons and the dwelling case study are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix C.1 specifies three generations, majority-label selection and random selection of a corresponding reason. v3 omits this repeated-generation information without specifying a replacement. Evaluator correlations and human inter-annotator agreement remain unchanged; fewer actual runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. Appendix E.3 newly reports example-specific ATRIE versus Direct Interpretation scores, including accuracy of 8.0 versus 6.5 and informativeness of 7.5 versus 6.5, and reports no fabricated ATRIE cases in that example.

T1.justification: The formal interpretation and LCE task definitions retain their meaning. The expanded task explanation and doctrinal background introduce no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Although the title and opening frame the work more broadly as legal interpretation, v3 explicitly retains concept interpretation as its focus. The central ATRIE, LCE and expert-comparable-quality contributions, including the remaining accuracy gap, are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E.3 adds explanations linking higher scores to quantified legal criteria, formal terminology and grounded examples, while identifying possible hallucination risks in Direct Interpretation. Section 5.7.1 adds a rationale for LCE as a quality proxy. Existing sample-size, leakage and human-oversight limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a public code/dataset statement and repository pointer, and names Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as the fact summarizer in Section 6.3. Most implementation information moves from Appendix C.1 to Section 5.6, but the voting and reason-selection details are omitted.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands the disciplinary context through a dedicated doctrinal legal research subsection covering its history, goals, methodology and relationship to Legal AI. It adds supporting literature and the LLM interpretation studies by Hoffman and Arbel and Engel and McAdams, while retaining the earlier research comparisons.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title, affiliations and introductory framing, standardizes terminology, expands related work and the task explanation, and moves implementation details into the main text. These are targeted revisions within the retained overall method-and-evaluation narrative.

P2.justification: Figures 1-4 and Tables 1-15 retain their displays, with minor caption wording and placement changes. For example, Figure 2 shifts columns, Table 4 appears alongside its ablation discussion, and Table 12 moves within the legal-LLM discussion. No new numbered displays are introduced.

improvement.justification: The new expert case study makes human scores more interpretable, while expanded context and code/data access information improve documentation. However, v3 removes the three-generation voting and reason-selection specification while retaining the same benchmark results, leaving their exact reproduction ambiguous. These benefits and the loss of a central evaluation detail prevent a confident net quality judgment.
